title: When does a statutory hearing require APA formal procedure?
shortTitle: When does a statutory hearing require APA formal procedure?
summary: A hearing mandate must be interpreted with the APA, the organic statute, the nature of the decision, and any special procedural provisions.
notes:
Formal APA procedure applies when an adjudication is required by statute to be determined on the record after opportunity for an agency hearing, subject to the statute’s exceptions. The practical inquiry has four parts: whether a hearing is required; whether that hearing triggers the APA; whether the organic act changes or adds procedures; and what procedure applies if a hearing is required but formal APA provisions are not. A separate statute can supply a specially tailored system, as the assigned discussion of Marcello v. Bonds illustrates.

Florida East Coast Railway construes general rulemaking hearing language without presuming a trial. Marathon Oil takes a different approach to individualized permit adjudication and emphasizes the substantive character of the inquiry. The notes report disagreement among circuits, including City of West Chicago’s use of the anti-formality approach and Seacoast’s former pro-formality rule. Chemical Waste and Dominion Energy subsequently relied on Chevron to defer to agency interpretations of hearing language. The assigned 2025 text notes that Loper Bright’s rejection of Chevron casts that rationale into doubt without predicting a definitive replacement rule for all hearing statutes. An agency’s special role administering its organic statute also differs from expertise over the generally applicable APA.
